the-purgatory-of-st-patrick: Spain's great dramatist Calderón de la Barca dramatizes the medieval legend of Saint Patrick's Purgatory, a cave in Ireland said to open onto the afterlife. A sinner descends into its visions of torment and mercy, emerging transformed. Mixing spectacular stage effects with deep questions of guilt and forgiveness, the play shows Calderón's religious imagination at full power.
the-legends-of-saint-patrick: Aubrey de Vere, the Irish poet, gathers the legends of Saint Patrick — the snakes, the shamrock, the contests with druids — in reverent verse. His poems keep alive the saint's place in Ireland's heart. Beautiful, devout work from a master of the sacred lyric. De Vere's reverent lines keep the patron saint's wonders green in memory.
to-infidelity-and-back: Henry F. Lutz tells how he went to infidelity and back — a thinking man's journey from doubt to faith regained. His honest, searching account has helped many doubters find their way. A moving testimony of return, plainly told. Honest doubt, fairly faced, led him home to faith.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-van-d: This 1913 reference piece on Abraham van Diepenbeeck — the Flemish painter, pupil of Rubens. Augustus Van Cleef traces his career. Churches and palaces hold his designs. A worthy heir of the great Peter Paul. His designs graced the Plantin press books.
